subject: Hosted API pricing qualification: token volume & peak TPS
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emma Harris <emma@britechanalytics.com>
Cc: procurement@britechanalytics.com, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-07-15T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: Hosted API pricing qualification: token volume & peak TPS

Hi Emma —

Thanks again for the time today — appreciate the candid discussion on your roadmap for adding LLM features to the Insights product. Quick recap and a few follow-ups so we can size Hosted API pricing:

Call recap (TL;DR)
- Primary use: conversational insights + on-demand summarization for analyst workflows.
- Traffic profile: mix of short chat requests (~150-300 tokens) and periodic long summarization jobs (~2,000 tokens).
- Key asks: predictable monthly spend, predictable peak TPS for SLOs, SOC2/compliance evidence.

To finalize a scoped hosted pricing estimate we need:
1) Expected monthly token volume (total input + output tokens) — ballpark is fine (e.g., 10M / 50M / 200M).
2) Peak TPS (concurrent token/sec requests or peak requests/sec) during business hours — helps us size burst capacity.
3) Target unit economics: range you’re aiming for ($ per 1M tokens) or an overall monthly budget for model inference.

From our side, to give you a usable estimate we typically map your volume + peak TPS to a blended $/1M tokens range and show options (hosted baseline, small reserved burst, or plan with caching to lower costs). If it helps, teams of your size often target $10–$30 per 1M tokens on hosted plans depending on model selection and whether we enable aggressive caching/quantization.

Can you send the ballpark numbers for (1) monthly tokens and (2) peak TPS? If you want, a quick follow-up call with Logan (cc’d, our solutions engineer) would let us validate assumptions for the SMUs and summarization batch sizes.

Next steps:
- You: ballpark monthly tokens + peak TPS + any budget guardrails
- Us: hosted pricing estimate + small model/throughput plan and SOC2 questionnaire (attached)

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwoodinference.com
(415) 555-0124

Attachment: Britech_SOC2_questionnaire.pdf (see attached)

From: Emma Harris <emma@britechanalytics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Britech Analytics Procurement <procurement@britechanalytics.com>
Date: 2026-07-16T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing qualification: token volume & peak TPS

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap. Quick answers from our side (ballpark):
- Expected monthly token volume (input+output): ~35,000,000 tokens/month. This includes chat + periodic batch summaries (~10% of volume is long-form summarization).
- Peak TPS: we currently see peak request rates around 15–25 reqs/sec during analyst-heavy hours; the summarisations are batched (so token density spikes) — if you prefer TPS in token/sec, assume ~300–500 tokens/sec at peak.
- Budget: initial pilot budget is ~$2,500/month but if unit economics look favorable we can increase after pilot (target is to be under $20 per 1M tokens for production).

We reviewed the SOC2 questionnaire you attached — procurement will own the formal submission. Looping them in for timeline.

Can Logan confirm whether we should be modeling token/sec or requests/sec for pricing math? We care about both latency SLOs and predictable monthly cost.

—Emma
Emma Harris
Head of AI, Britech Analytics
emma@britechanalytics.com

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emma Harris <emma@britechanalytics.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@britechanalytics.com
Date: 2026-07-16T11:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing qualification: token volume & peak TPS

Emma —

This is helpful, thanks. A couple quick clarifications to make the hosted estimate accurate:
- For pricing we usually present both: blended $/1M tokens (monthly) and a recommended peak capacity (peak TPS in tokens/sec) that determines burst capacity needed for latency SLOs.
- Based on your mix (35M/mo with ~10% long summaries) I’d model ~450–500 tokens/sec peak to be safe if you want <1s tail latency on short chat paths during peak. If you can tolerate slightly higher latency for long summaries we can size lower.
- Unit economics note: our hosted plan examples map like this (illustrative):
  - $12–$18 per 1M tokens if you enable caching + use a smaller, cheaper generation model for short chats
  - $22–$35 per 1M tokens for higher-quality/latency-optimized model choices without aggressive caching

Given your initial pilot budget ~$2.5k/month and 35M tokens/month, that implies target unit cost ~ $71/1M tokens (35M tokens -> 35 * $/1M = $2,500, so $/1M ≈ $71). That’s above the ranges where we'd recommend production usage; so for pilot we can propose a constrained plan:
  1) Pilot approach: cap usage to a subset of users or enable more aggressive caching/response length limits to bring effective tokens down to ~5–10M tokens/mo during pilot.
  2) Alternative: keep 35M usage but provide a promotional pilot rate/credits to bridge the delta while we demonstrate value.

If you can confirm whether the $2.5k/month is a hard cap for the pilot (vs. expected to expand), we’ll prepare two concrete options: (A) constrained/optimized pilot design that fits $2.5k or (B) full-volume hosted estimate with suggested unit-cost targets and reserved-capacity options.

Happy to jump on a 30-min call to walk through model tradeoffs and run the simple cost model together — I’m available tomorrow 10–12 PT.

—Logan
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
logan_wright@redwoodinference.com

Emma / Procurement —

Thanks for the quick answers and Logan for the helpful breakdown. Next steps from us:
- I’ll put together two written options and ballpark pricing by EOD tomorrow:
  Option A: Pilot (fits $2.5k/mo) — constrained volume (5–10M effective tokens) + caching + conservative summary lengths; includes 1 month of promotional credits.
  Option B: Production estimate (35M/mo) — hosted list-rate estimate + recommended peak capacity (~500 tokens/sec) and potential discount tiers if usage grows.
- Logan will join a short call if you want to walk the numbers live (Logan available tomorrow 10–12 PT).
- Procurement: we’ll mark SOC2 questionnaire as submitted; expect an email summary linking the DocuSign MSA and HubSpot record (HS-987654).

If procurement could confirm whether $2.5k is a hard pilot cap, that will determine the option we prioritize.
